An arbitrary embedded nonclosed Z need not have locally finite density mass. For G=X=R, the disjoint lines x-g=1/j, j>=1, form an embedded submanifold with both projections submersions. Put |dg| on each line. A nonnegative compact test equal to one on [-1,1] times [-2,2] has infinite integral, since every line contributes at least 2. Ambient local finiteness is now required, and Proof 1.3 proves absolute convergence and continuity. This excludes precisely the unsupported integrals without requiring every Z to be closed.
